about: Numbers for web/proof.html, computed by tools/make_proof.mjs from the app pipeline (data.js) on cached SPHEREx cutouts. AI-written code (Claude, Anthropic) for team Proper Motion, NASA Space Apps 2026.

motion: the measured motion is within 2 uncertainties (2σ) of the catalogue, and the uncertainty is no more than half the value.
between 2σ and 3σ, or the uncertainty is larger than half the value.
more than 3σ from the catalogue. Shown as measured, with the likely reason.
the catalogue motion moves the star less than one 6.15″ pixel over the dates we have, or the fit could not run.
brightness: the catalogue calls it a variable star, and we see its brightness change by more than 3σ between the first and last season, in at least one of the two wavelength groups.
the change is under 3σ: no clear change above the noise.
too few images where the star's centre is unmasked and the wavelengths match.

tests.limit: The star's centre is flagged saturated in 120 of 120 images, so its centre is found from the unsaturated edge pixels. The long-wavelength detectors alone give 10.61 ± 0.20″/yr, the short ones 9.44 ± 0.83″/yr.

Epsilon Indi A is 6.7′ away, outside this 2.6′ patch, and no image has scattered-light flags near B; hiding every flagged image gives 4.28 ± 0.09″/yr. The value comes out 7% slow, like Barnard's Star: the error bar is statistical only and leaves out a centroid bias on 6.15″ pixels.

expected.source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, Spitzer + WISE (via SIMBAD)

tests.limit: Faint at short wavelengths: only the two longest bands (detectors 5–6, 3.8–5.0 µm) were used. With detectors 1–4 the fit gives 0.20 ± 0.44″/yr, because it locks on a background star (Gaia G 16.31) 7.8″ away that does not move.
The catalogue motion (0.02″/yr) moves it only 0.022″ (0.004 of a 6.15″ pixel) over the 1.0 years of images, far below what one pixel can show.

expected.text: T Tauri star (young, varies irregularly). No fixed period.

tests.limit: Only images with no masked pixel within 15″ of the star count, each compared with first-season images from the same detector at the same wavelength: 64 of 120 images qualify (16 have a saturated, masked centre; the rest have no first-season match). The catalogue gives no amplitude at these wavelengths, so only the fact of a change is tested. Control: on Barnard's Star, a steady star, the season averages stay within 0.05 mag of the first season (only 15 of its 120 images have an unmasked centre).
The catalogue motion (0.02″/yr) moves it only 0.021″ (0.003 of a 6.15″ pixel) over the 1.2 years of images, far below what one pixel can show.

expected.text: Mira variable (pulsating red giant). Period 247.2 days.
expected.source: SIMBAD type; period from Gaia DR3 variability

tests.limit: Too bright for SPHEREx: in 120 of 120 images the centre pixels are saturated and masked, leaving 0 usable comparisons, too few to measure a change.
